6828-the-works-of-henry-fielding-vol-12.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. that's fit, on Liberty, freedom, liberty and Briton! While frowning, gaping for applause he stands, What generous Briton can refuse his hands? Like the tame animals design'd for show, You have your cues to clap, as they to bow, Taught to commend, your judgments have no share, By chance you guess aright, by chance you err.

arxiv-2008-03097.title: Electromagnetic field theory for invariant beams using scalar potentials
arxiv-2008-03097.creator: Irving Rondón, F. Soto-Eguibar
arxiv-2008-03097.description: Abstract We present a description of the electromagnetic field for propagation invariant beams using scalar potentials. Fundamental dynamical quantities are obtained: the energy density, the Poynting vector and the Maxwell stress tensor. As an example, all these quantities are explicitly calculated for the Bessel beams, which are the invariant beams with circular cylindrical symmetry.

arxiv-2208-03510.title: Two-loop mixed QCD-EW corrections to neutral current Drell-Yan
arxiv-2208-03510.description: Abstract We present the mixed QCD-EW two-loop virtual amplitudes for the neutral current Drell-Yan production, one of the bottlenecks for the complete calculation of the NNLO mixed QCD-EW corrections. We present the computational details and the first steps towards their automation.

arxiv-2210-06671.title: Wasserstein Barycenter-based Model Fusion and Linear Mode Connectivity of Neural Networks
arxiv-2210-06671.creator: Aditya Kumar Akash Department of Computer ScienceUniversity of Wisconsin-Madison aakash@wisc.edu Sixu Li Department of StatisticsUniversity of Wisconsin-Madison sli739@wisc.edu Nicolás García TrillosDepartment of StatisticsUniversity of Wisconsin-Madison garciatrillo@wisc.edu
arxiv-2210-06671.description: Abstract Based on the concepts of Wasserstein barycenter (WB) and Gromov-Wasserstein barycenter (GWB), we propose a unified mathematical framework for neural network (NN) model fusion and utilize it to reveal new insights about the linear mode connectivity of SGD solutions.

arxiv-2302-08310.title: Wireless Communications with Space-Time Modulated Metasurfaces
arxiv-2302-08310.creator: Marouan Mizmizi, Dario Tagliaferri, Umberto Spagnolini
arxiv-2302-08310.description: Abstract Space-time modulated metasurfaces (STMMs) are a newly investigated technology for the next 6G generation wireless communication networks. An STMM augments the spatial phase function with a time-varying one across the meta-atoms, allowing for the conveyance of information that possibly modulates the impinging signal.

arxiv-2302-10298.title: Quantum Machine Learning hyperparameter search
arxiv-2302-10298.creator: S. Consul-Pacareu, R. Montaño, Kevin Rodriguez-Fernandez, Àlex Corretgé, Esteve Vilella-Moreno, Daniel Casado-Faulí, Parfait Atchade-Adelomou
arxiv-2302-10298.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by S. Consul-Pacareu, R. Montaño, Kevin Rodriguez-Fernandez, Àlex Corretgé, Esteve Vilella-Moreno, Daniel Casado-Faulí, Parfait Atchade-Adelomou. This paper presents a quantum-based Fourier-regression approach for machine learning hyperparameter optimization applied to a benchmark of models trained on a dataset related to a forecast problem in the airline industry. Our approach utilizes the Fourier series method to represent the hyperparameter search space, which is then optimized using quantum algorithms to find the optimal set of hyperparameters for a given machine learning model.

arxiv-2401-15297.title: A smart granular intruder
arxiv-2401-15297.creator: Lázaro Martínez-Ortíz, Alex Rivera-Rivera, Ernesto Altshuler ∗
arxiv-2401-15297.description: Abstract It has been recently reported that irregular objects sink irregularly when released in a granular medium: a subtle lack of symmetry in the density or shape of a macroscopic object may produce a large tilting and deviation from the vertical path when released from the free surface of a granular bed.

arxiv-2409-04909.title: Efficient Training of Transformers for Molecule Property Prediction on Small-scale Datasets
arxiv-2409-04909.creator: Shivesh Prakash
arxiv-2409-04909.description: Abstract The blood-brain barrier (BBB) serves as a protective barrier that separates the brain from the circulatory system, regulating the passage of substances into the central nervous system. Assessing the BBB permeability of potential drugs is crucial for effective drug targeting. However, traditional experimental methods for measuring BBB permeability are challenging and impractical for large-scale screening.

arxiv-2409-17259.title: The Magellanic Clouds are very rare in the IllustrisTNG simulations
arxiv-2409-17259.creator: Moritz Haslbauer, Indranil Banik*, Pavel Kroupa, Hongsheng Zhao, Elena Asencio
arxiv-2409-17259.description: Abstract The Large and Small Magellanic Cloud (LMC and SMC) form the closest interacting galactic system to the Milky Way, therewith providing a laboratory to test cosmological models in the local Universe. We quantify the likelihood for the Magellanic Clouds (MCs) to be observed within the Λ \Lambda CDM model using hydrodynamical simulations of the IllustrisTNG project.

arxiv-2410-10076.title: VideoAgent: Self-Improving Video Generation for Embodied Planning
arxiv-2410-10076.creator: Achint Soni, Sreyas Venkataraman, Abhranil Chandra, Sebastian Fischmeister, Percy Liang, Bo Dai, Sherry Yang
arxiv-2410-10076.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Achint Soni, Sreyas Venkataraman, Abhranil Chandra, Sebastian Fischmeister, Percy Liang, Bo Dai, Sherry Yang. Video generation has been used to generate visual plans for controlling robotic systems. Given an image observation and a language instruction, previous work has generated video plans which are then converted to robot controls to be executed.

arxiv-2506-00613.title: Evaluating Robot Policies in a World Model
arxiv-2506-00613.creator: Julian Quevedo 1, Percy Liang 1, Sherry Yang 1 2 3, New York University 2, Google DeepMind 3
arxiv-2506-00613.description: Abstract Robotics has broad applications from automating house chores to taking care of patients. However, evaluating robot control policies is challenging, as real-world testing is expensive, while handcrafted simulations often fail to accurately reflect real-world conditions, resulting in poor correlation between simulated evaluation and real-world outcomes. In this work, we investigate World-model-based Policy Evaluation (WPE).

arxiv-2602-02555.title: Learning to Explore with Parameter-Space Noise: A Deep Dive into Parameter-Space Noise for Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards
arxiv-2602-02555.creator: Bizhe Bai, Xinyue Wang, Peng Ye, Tao Chen
arxiv-2602-02555.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Bizhe Bai, Xinyue Wang, Peng Ye, Tao Chen. Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) improves LLM reasoning, yet growing evidence indicates an exploration ceiling : it often reweights existing solution traces rather than discovering new strategies, limiting gains under large sampling budgets (e.g., pass@ 256). We address this limitation with PSN-RLVR , which perturbs policy parameters before rollout generation to induce temporally consistent, trajectory-level exploration that better preserves long-horizon chain-of-thought coherence than action-space noise.

europmc-pmc7617101.title: Body-mass index and obesity in urban and rural China: findings from consecutive nationally representative surveys during 2004-18.
europmc-pmc7617101.creator: Wang L, Zhou B, Zhao Z, Yang L, Zhang M, Jiang Y, Li Y, Zhou M, Wang L, Huang Z, Zhang X, Zhao L, Yu D, Li C, Ezzati M, Chen Z, Wu J, Ding G, Li X.
europmc-pmc7617101.description: Background In China, mean body-mass index (BMI) and obesity in adults have increased steadily since the early 1980s. However, to our knowledge, there has been no reliable assessment of recent trends, nationally, regionally, or in certain population subgroups. To address this evi

europmc-pmc8507252.title: Exosomal miR-30d-5p of neutrophils induces M1 macrophage polarization and primes macrophage pyroptosis in sepsis-related acute lung injury.
europmc-pmc8507252.creator: Jiao Y, Zhang T, Zhang C, Ji H, Tong X, Xia R, Wang W, Ma Z, Shi X.
europmc-pmc8507252.description: Background Polymorphonuclear neutrophils (PMNs) play an important role in sepsis-related acute lung injury (ALI). Accumulating evidence suggests PMN-derived exosomes as a new subcellular entity acting as a fundamental link between PMN-driven inflammation and tissue damage. Howev

pmc-10560765.title: Evaluation of the Diagnostic Performance of the LINEAR Cromatest and Laboquick URS 10-T Dipsticks Among Urinary Tract Infection Suspects in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia: A Cross-Sectional Study
pmc-10560765.creator: Yosef Gebretensaie, Abay Atnafu, Yonas Alemu, Selfu Girma, Kassu Desta
pmc-10560765.description: BackgroundUrinary tract infections (UTIs) bring a significant and serious health-related problem. Repeated infections may lead to the development of renal scarring and end-stage renal dysfunction. Therefore, balancing the choices of UTI diagnostic tools depending on the costs versus accuracy can minimize false results that may subject patients to wrong treatments.

pmc-10655755.title: Clinical Profile and Outcomes of Rheumatic Heart Disease Patients Undergoing Surgical Valve Procedures in Uganda
pmc-10655755.creator: Joselyn Rwebembera, Andrew Y. Chang, Samalie M. Kitooleko, Gloria Kaudha, Sarah de Loizaga, Miriam Nalule, Kenneth Ahabwe, Wanzhu Zhang, Emmy Okello, Pranava Sinha, Tom Mwambu, Craig Sable, Andrea Beaton, Chris T. Longenecker
pmc-10655755.description: Background:Chronic valvular heart disease is a well-known, long-term complication of acute rheumatic fever (ARF), which remains a major public health problem in low- and middle-income countries. Access to surgical management remains limited. Outcomes of the minority proportion of patients that access surgery have not been described in Uganda.

pmc-11710651.title: Subjective Cognitive Complaints: Heritability and Correlations with Dementia Diagnosis, Depression and Memory, Across Multiple Twin Studies
pmc-11710651.creator: Ashleigh S. Vella, Amanda Selwood, Vibeke S. Catts, Katya T. Numbers, Teresa Lee, Anbupalam Thalamuthu, Ida K Karlsson, Chandra A. Reynolds, Carol E. Franz, William S. Kremen, Margaret Gatz, Perminder S. Sachdev
pmc-11710651.description: BackgroundSubjective Cognitive Complaints (SCCs) can often precede mild cognitive impairment and dementia longitudinally. While increasingly considered an early prodromal stage of dementia, SCCs can also be a symptom of depression. Previous research found that SCCs in the absence of cognitive impairment, controlling for symptoms of depression, were moderately heritable and genetically associated with memory.

pmc-11738806.title: Two Years Beyond COVID-19: Unveiling the Persistence of Neuropsychiatric Symptoms and Risk Factors in a Cross-Sectional Study
pmc-11738806.creator: Poulami Laha, Guru S Gowda, V Senthil Kumar Reddi, Harish T, Sydney Moirangthem
pmc-11738806.description: AimsThe neuropsychiatric morbidities associated with post-COVID status are important public health issues. The range and severity of morbidity varies with the type of clinical setting and time of assessment. There are limited studies on the long-term persistence of the post-COVID neuropsychiatric symptoms (PCNS).

pmc-11786209.title: Clinicopathologic Effects of Xenogeneic GvHD Induced by Adoptively Transferred Human-Derived T Cells in Severely Immunodeficient Mice
pmc-11786209.creator: Hami Ashraf, Farid Kosari, Amir Arsalan Khorsand, Samad Muhammadnejad, Vahid Mansouri, Ahad Muhammadnejad, Naser Ahmadbeigi, Seyed Mostafa Monzavi
pmc-11786209.description: Background: Xenogeneic graft-versus-host disease (xGvHD) is an inevitable confounder of preclinical evaluation of adoptive immunotherapies on tumor-bearing immunodeficient mouse models. This study was designed to appraise the clinical and histopathological effects caused by xGvHD in severely immunodeficient mice considering the T cell dosage.

pmc-12474431.title: Machine Learning-Based Detection of Pig Coughs and Their Association with Respiratory Diseases in Fattening Pigs
pmc-12474431.creator: Panuwat Yamsakul, Terdsak Yano, Kiettipoch Junchum, Wichittra Anukool, Nattinee Kittiwan
pmc-12474431.description: Simple SummaryRespiratory problems in pigs are one of the important issues in pig farming, as they can affect both animal health and the overall productivity of the farm. Coughing is one of the noticeable symptoms and can be either productive or non-productive, but in practice, distinguishing between the two types can be difficult and often depends on the person’s experience.

pmc-12613399.title: Reflections on the impact of the Lived Experience Group in the James Lind Alliance Palliative and End of Life Care Priority Setting Partnership Refresh
pmc-12613399.creator: Jessica Bush, Jodie Crooks, Anna Dawson, Rashmi Kumar, Alexandra Reece, Diana Robinson, Sabine Best, Briony Hudson
pmc-12613399.description: BackgroundIn 2025, Marie Curie and other partners launched the results of a refreshed Priority Setting Partnership with the James Lind Alliance, to identify priorities for palliative and end of life care research, based on the views of people affected by serious life limiting illness.

pmc-12764116.title: Examining the impact of naming equity within perinatal substance use and mental health policy: a scoping review
pmc-12764116.creator: Sana Z Shahram, Lisa Knox, Megan Black, Alex Kent, Bernie Pauly, Lenora Marcellus
pmc-12764116.description: The ways in which we understand and respond to perinatal substance use are explicitly and implicitly driven by policy. Perinatal substance use is a visible manifestation of intersecting systems of oppression, shaped by racist, colonial and sexist discourses surrounding mothering and drug use. Policies related to perinatal substance use and mental health have far-reaching impacts on families, communities and generations.

pmc-13055743.title: Statin Use and Recurrent Atherosclerotic Cardiovascular Disease Events in Patients With Coronary Artery Intervention: A Retrospective Analysis From a Large Health Care Network
pmc-13055743.creator: Omair Ahmed, Jianhui Zhu, Floyd Thoma, Agnes Koczo, Oscar C. Marroquin, Suresh R. Mulukutla, Salim S. Virani, Anum Saeed
pmc-13055743.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundAtherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) poses a significant health challenge worldwide. While statins effectively reduce low‐density lipoprotein (LDL) cholesterol and lower cardiovascular risk, patients with coronary artery disease who undergo revascularization remain vulnerable to recurrent ASCVD events.

pmc-13340951.title: Occupational disease “Skin cancer caused by UV radiation” – unambiguous facts, heterogeneous consequences
pmc-13340951.creator: Werner Aberer, Rainer Hofmann‐Wellenhof, Norbert Sepp, Barbara Ebner, Swen‐Malte John
pmc-13340951.description: s an increasing occupational health challenge, especially in outdoor work. Despite alarming incidence rates and clear scientific evidence regarding its etiology, SCC and its precursors are not recognized as an occupational disease in many countries. Legislative measures vary greatly – from complete neglect to the establishment of comprehensive prevention and compensation programs.

pmc-13341923.title: Disrupted functional connectivity during stroke recovery revealed via bedside optical neuroimaging
pmc-13341923.creator: Karla M. Bergonzi, Broc A. Burke, Morgan Fogarty, Arefeh Sherafati, Tracy M. Burns-Yocum, Silvina L. Ferradal, Ben Julian A. Palanca, Rajat Dhar, Gyanendra Kumar, Jin-Moo Lee, Joseph P. Culver, Adam T. Eggebrecht
pmc-13341923.description: .SignificanceCurrent clinical care following ischemic stroke provides intermittent assessments, potentially missing early detection of neurological deterioration. Optical imaging offers the potential for a continuous, portable alternative to the current combination of physical exams and radiological imaging. However, optical imaging technology has lacked the crucial combination of portability, resolution, and coverage required to assess spatially distributed brain function.

pmc-13651455.title: Association between socioeconomic status and dental caries in adolescents – a systematic review of cohort studies
pmc-13651455.creator: Marit Slåttelid Skeie, Kristin Solveig Klock, Göran Dahllöf, Hedda Høvik, Ida Sofie Karlsen Sletten, Tone Natland Fagerhaug, Abhijit Sen
pmc-13651455.description: IntroductionEarly adolescence is a critical period for caries initiation, underlining the need for updated knowledge on effective caries indicators. This systematic review of cohort studies aimed to assess the association between socioeconomic status (SES), involving a wide range of indicators, and dental caries in adolescents aged 12–19.

uslaw-usc-t7-s7237.title: 7 U.S.C. § 7237 — Availability of recourse loans for high moisture feed grains and seed cotton and other fibers
uslaw-usc-t7-s7237.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t7-s7237.description: United States Code, Title 7 (Agriculture); Chapter 100 (Agricultural Market Transition); Subchapter III (Nonrecourse Marketing Assistance Loans And Loan Deficiency Payments). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) High moisture feed grains (1) Recourse loans available For each of the 1996 through 2002 crops of corn and grain sorghum, the Secretary shall make available recourse loans, as determined by the Secretary, to producers.
